_comment: feature -> version -> FR in one write-srs run. The order matters: a page can only reference a logical id declared before it in the batch. A version's items (nfrItems) and an FR candidate's items (urs, dsItems, tcItems) are listed in the feature's tables with the version (#900). To add a version to a feature written earlier, set the version's parentId to that feature page's URL or id (#899).

epic.title: Réunion live : transcript & notes
epic.businessValue: A participant follows a meeting without taking notes by hand, and leaves with a usable record of it.
epic.scope: Live transcript and AI notes during a meeting, and the record kept afterwards. Scheduling and recording consent stay out of scope.

candidates._comment: A version. `parentId` is what makes it one — position decides the level, never the title. Call it MVP, V1 or 'v2 — Titre'; the tooling reads where it sits.

changes: Notes are grouped by topic rather than appended chronologically.
A foreign-language passage is summarised in the meeting's language.

nfrItems.title: Topic notes stay readable during the meeting
nfrItems.target: Notes refresh ≤ 2 s after a topic change (p95)

candidates._comment: FRs attach to the VERSION, never to the feature. An FR pointing at FEAT-LIVE here is refused: Epic = feature + version.

fr.title: Topic-aware AI note taking
fr.description: Live notes are grouped under the topic being discussed rather than appended in order of arrival.
acceptanceCriteria: A topic change creates a new group.
A note arriving after a topic change lands under the new topic.

urs.narrative: The participant sees the notes grouped by the topic being discussed

dsItems.title: Topic segmentation of the transcript
dsItems.description: The transcript is cut into topic segments as it streams; notes attach to the open segment.

tcItems.title: Notes follow the topic
tcItems.expectedResult: Three topic groups of notes, in order
